simple.meaning: נָבַח (nâbach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bark (as a dog).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 56:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָבַח (H5024) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H5024. nabach [ נָבַח ] verb bark (of dogs) (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic ; Ethiopic ; Aramaic , נְבַח ); — Qal Infinitive construct only לִנְבֹּחַ יוּכְלוּ לֹא אִלְּמִים כְּלָבִים כֻּלָּם Isa 56:10 figurative of helpless prophets.
